source_evidence.anchor: Section 2 floating-point model and componentwise convention
source_evidence.observation: The paper considers Ax=b with n equations and n unknowns, assumes a positive relative-roundoff bound u with nu≤0.01, assumes every referenced floating-point operation is well defined, and declares absolute values and inequalities in the roundoff analysis to be componentwise.
Only absolute vector norms satisfying |||v|||=||v|| are considered; equivalently they are monotone. The norm is normalized by ||e_i||=1 and extended to row vectors and matrices in the usual way.
The paper defines the nonstandard quantity κ(A^{-1})=|| |A| |A^{-1}| || and explicitly warns that κ is not a norm-defined condition number.
Lower-case c_i and upper-case C_i denote positive scalar and matrix quantities, respectively, which are bounded above by functions of n only.
A column-pivoted solve produces an approximation satisfying |A x_hat-b|≤u C_2 |A| |x| under c_1uκ(A^{-1})≤1/2, where c_1=||C_1|| and C_2=(I-uC_1|A||A^{-1}|)^{-1}C_1.

The algorithm computes x_1 by column pivoting and, for m≥1, computes r_m as Ax_m-b, computes d_m as A^{-1}r_m by column pivoting, and performs the floating-point update x_{m+1}=fl(x_m-d_m). It defines x_0=0, r_0=-b, d_0=-x_1. Residual subtraction is last; s.p.r.a. uses single precision, while d.p.r.a. uses double precision followed by conversion to single precision.
The exact residual is q_{m+1}=A(x_m-d_m)-b. Lemma 4.1 bounds it using bar_u=u for s.p.r.a. and bar_u=u^2 for d.p.r.a.
The page defines c_3,c_4,c_5,C_6,C_7 and gives |x_{m+1}-x|≤(1+u)|A^{-1}||q_{m+1}|+u|x|, the forward-error estimate substituted into Lemma 4.1.

source_evidence.anchor: Lemma 4.3, following Note, and proof recurrence
source_evidence.observation: Lemma 4.3 states the selected four-term finite componentwise bound, assumes c_8uκ(A^{-1})≤1/2, defines C_8 through C_12 and c_8, and derives the result by induction from a displayed one-step recurrence.

binders: Fix n≥1, an n-by-n system Ax=b, and the exact solution x=A^{-1}b; nonsingularity of A is inherited from the repeated use of A^{-1}. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 818, anchor: Section 2 opening; PDF p. 8, printed p. 823, anchor: equation (3.1)]

Fix a positive working-precision roundoff bound u and one residual mode, s.p.r.a. or d.p.r.a. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 818, anchor: floating-point model; PDF p. 9, printed p. 824, anchor: residual-precision paragraph]

For every integer m=0,1,2,..., Lemma 4.3 bounds q_{m+1}. Thus n,A,b,u, the residual mode, and the defined constants precede the universal quantification over m. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Lemma 4.3]
hypotheses: The standing arithmetic restriction is nu≤0.01, and every floating-point operation referenced by the computation is assumed well defined. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 818, anchor: Section 2 floating-point model]
The iterates and corrections are those of the stated iterative-refinement algorithm using Gaussian elimination with column pivoting. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 824, anchor: Section 4 algorithm]

The explicit hypothesis of Lemma 4.3 is c_8 u κ(A^{-1})≤1/2, where c_8=||C_8|| and κ(A^{-1})=|| |A| |A^{-1}| ||. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Lemma 4.3 and Note; PDF p. 5, printed p. 820, anchor: definition of κ(A^{-1})]
conclusions: For every m=0,1,2,..., |q_{m+1}| ≤ (u C_8 |A| |A^{-1}|)^m u C_10 |A| |x| + n bar_u |A| |x| + u^2 C_11 |A| |x| + bar_u u C_12 |A| |A^{-1}| |A| |x|. This is one componentwise inequality with exactly four additive terms. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Lemma 4.3]
definitions_and_conventions: x=A^{-1}b is exact, whereas x_m and d_m are computed floating-point quantities generated by the algorithm. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 823, anchor: column-pivoted approximation to x=A^{-1}b; PDF p. 9, printed p. 824, anchor: Section 4 algorithm]

q_{m+1}=A(x_m-d_m)-b is the exact residual of the unrounded mathematical difference x_m-d_m; it is distinct from the computed residual r_m and from the rounded update x_{m+1}. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 825, anchor: paragraph preceding and statement of Lemma 4.1; PDF p. 9, printed p. 824, anchor: algorithm]
bar_u=u for s.p.r.a. and bar_u=u^2 for d.p.r.a. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 825, anchor: Lemma 4.1]

|A|, |A^{-1}|, |x|, and |q_{m+1}| are componentwise absolute values, and every displayed ≤ between vectors is componentwise. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 818, anchor: componentwise convention; PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Lemma 4.3]

I denotes the n-by-n identity; upper-case C_i are matrices and lower-case c_i are scalars. [PDF p. 7, printed p. 822, anchor: anonymous-quantity convention; PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Note following Lemma 4.3]
The power (uC_8|A||A^{-1}|)^m is a matrix power acting on uC_10|A||x|; at m=0 the standard zeroth-power interpretation gives the identity matrix. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Lemma 4.3]
implicit_context: The column-pivoted solve certificate inherited from (3.1) is |A x_hat-b|≤uC_2|A||x| under c_1uκ(A^{-1})≤1/2; in Lemma 4.1 it is applied to d_m with exact solve value A^{-1}r_m. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 823, anchor: equation (3.1); PDF p. 11, printed p. 826, anchor: proof of Lemma 4.1]
Lemma 4.1 supplies |q_{m+1}|≤uC_6|A||x_m-x|+(n bar_u+c_3u^2)|A||x|+bar_u u C_7|A||A^{-1}||A||x|. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 825, anchor: Lemma 4.1]
Lemma 4.2 supplies |x_{m+1}-x|≤(1+u)|A^{-1}||q_{m+1}|+u|x|. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 826, anchor: Lemma 4.2]

For the induction step, substitution yields |q_{m+1}|≤uC_8|A||A^{-1}||q_m|+n bar_u|A||x|+u^2C_9|A||x|+bar_u u C_7|A||A^{-1}||A||x| under c_1uκ(A^{-1})≤1/2. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: proof recurrence of Lemma 4.3]
The base case m=0 comes from Lemma 4.1, and subsequent cases follow by induction using the recurrence. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: final paragraph of Lemma 4.3 proof]
statement.algorithm_linkage: Column pivoting is the partial-pivoting variant that selects the largest element in the next column as pivot. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 818, anchor: Section 3 overview] The algorithm sets x_1 to the column-pivoted computed value of A^{-1}b; for m≥1 it computes r_m=fl(Ax_m-b), computes d_m by a column-pivoted solve for A^{-1}r_m, and sets x_{m+1}=fl(x_m-d_m). [PDF p. 9, printed p. 824, anchor: Section 4 algorithm] The artificial initialization x_0=0, r_0=-b, d_0=-x_1 makes q_1=Ax_1-b and permits the lemma's index range to begin at m=0. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 824, anchor: initialization; PDF p. 10, printed p. 825, anchor: definition of q_{m+1}]
numerical_model: Single-precision floating-point arithmetic has relative roundoff bounded by the positive number u, with nu≤0.01; the paper does not state a more detailed rounding rule. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 818, anchor: Section 2 floating-point model]

For s.p.r.a., Ax_m-b is accumulated in single precision. For d.p.r.a., it is accumulated in double precision, whose relative roundoff is bounded by u^2, and the result is then converted to single precision with relative conversion error bounded by u. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 824, anchor: residual-precision paragraph]
The residual subtraction is performed last in both modes. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 824, anchor: residual-precision paragraph]

The initial and correction solves retain the working-precision u certificate from column-pivoted Gaussian elimination in both residual modes; only residual accumulation changes through bar_u. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 823, anchor: equation (3.1); PDF p. 10, printed p. 825, anchor: Lemma 4.1]
error_notions: The bounded quantity is the componentwise magnitude of the exact residual q_{m+1}=A(x_m-d_m)-b, not the norm of a residual and not a backward-error scalar. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 825, anchor: definition of q_{m+1}; PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Lemma 4.3]

r_m is the computed residual and satisfies r_m=Ax_m-b+f_m; q_{m+1} instead measures the exact residual before rounding the update. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 826, anchor: equation (4.1) and proof of Lemma 4.1]

The componentwise forward error |x_m-x| is only an intermediate quantity eliminated through Lemma 4.2 to obtain the q-recurrence. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 825, anchor: Lemma 4.1; PDF p. 11, printed p. 826, anchor: Lemma 4.2; PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: proof of Lemma 4.3]
norms: The standing vector norm is absolute, so |||v|||=||v||, and therefore monotone: |v|≤|w| implies ||v||≤||w||. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 819, anchor: absolute monotone norm convention]

It is normalized by ||e_i||=1 for 1≤i≤n and extended to row vectors and matrices in the usual way; the paper also records ||v||_∞≤||v||≤||v||_1. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 819, anchor: norm normalization and extension]

κ(A^{-1}) means || |A| |A^{-1}| || in this norm. The order |A||A^{-1}| is essential, and κ is explicitly nonstandard rather than ||A||·||A^{-1}||. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 820, anchor: definition of κ(A^{-1})]

The scalar smallness factors are c_1=||C_1|| and c_8=||C_8||. The conclusion itself remains componentwise despite these norm-based hypotheses. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 823, anchor: Note after (3.1); PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Note after Lemma 4.3]
constants_and_indexing: The solve constants are c_1=||C_1|| and C_2=(I-uC_1|A||A^{-1}|)^{-1}C_1. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 823, anchor: Note following equation (3.1)]
For s.p.r.a., c_3=(1+u)[(1+u)^n-1]/u^2-n/u and c_4=0. For d.p.r.a., c_3=(1+u)(1+u^2)[(1+u^2)^n-1]/u^2-n and c_4=1+u. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 826, anchor: Note following Lemma 4.1]
c_5=n+(c_3+c_4)u^2/bar_u, C_6=C_2+(1+c_5 bar_u/u)(I+uC_2|A||A^{-1}|), and C_7=(n+c_3u^2/bar_u)C_2. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 826, anchor: Note following Lemma 4.1]
C_8=(1+u)C_6, c_8=||C_8||, and C_9=C_6+c_3I. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Note following Lemma 4.3]
C_10=C_6+(n bar_u/u+c_3u)I+bar_u C_7|A||A^{-1}|. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Note following Lemma 4.3]
C_11=(I-uC_8|A||A^{-1}|)^{-1}C_9 and C_12=(I-uC_8|A||A^{-1}|)^{-1}(nC_8+C_7). [PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Note following Lemma 4.3]

All c_i and C_i used here are asserted to be bounded above by functions of n only under the standing hypotheses; lower-case symbols are scalars and upper-case symbols are matrices. [PDF p. 7, printed p. 822, anchor: anonymous-quantity convention; PDF p. 11, printed p. 826, anchor: Note; PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Note]

The actual refinement loop begins at m=1, but x_0=0, r_0=-b, d_0=-x_1 extend the analysis to m=0. Consequently Lemma 4.3 at m=0 bounds q_1, and its matrix-power exponent is zero. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 824, anchor: algorithm initialization; PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Lemma 4.3]
higher_order_terms: Lemma 4.3 is a finite displayed inequality and contains no O(u^k) remainder or omitted term. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Lemma 4.3]

Under s.p.r.a., the second and fourth terms specialize to nu|A||x| and u^2C_12|A||A^{-1}||A||x|. Under d.p.r.a., they specialize to nu^2|A||x| and u^3C_12|A||A^{-1}||A||x|. The u^2C_11 term occurs in both modes. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 825, anchor: definition of bar_u; PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Lemma 4.3]
The first term retains an initial factor u in both modes and contains the full finite matrix power (uC_8|A||A^{-1}|)^m. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Lemma 4.3]

Higher-order dependence is also retained inside c_3 and the resolvent definitions of C_11 and C_12 rather than being discarded asymptotically. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 826, anchor: definition of c_3; PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: definitions of C_11 and C_12]
exceptional_values: The floating-point system is modeled as a subset of the reals, and every referenced operation is assumed well defined; NaNs, infinities, overflow behavior, underflow behavior, and subnormals are not separately modeled. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 818, anchor: Section 2 floating-point model]

Existence of A^{-1} is inherited from the problem and algorithm notation. The definitions of C_2,C_11,C_12 also require their displayed matrix inverses, with the associated smallness conditions controlling those resolvents. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 823, anchor: equation (3.1) and Note; PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Lemma 4.3 and Note]

Lemma 4.3 does not impose componentwise positivity of |A||x| or divide by its components; zero components are therefore not excluded by the displayed statement. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Lemma 4.3]

undebatable_constraints: The target result is the Lemma 4.3 bound on |q_{m+1}|, not either forward-error inequality of Theorem 4.4. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Lemma 4.3 and Theorem 4.4]
q_{m+1} must be defined exactly as A(x_m-d_m)-b, with ordinary unrounded subtraction inside this definition. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 825, anchor: Lemma 4.1]
The bound must contain all four terms and the first term must be (uC_8|A||A^{-1}|)^m uC_10|A||x|. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Lemma 4.3]
The second, third, and fourth terms must respectively be n bar_u|A||x|, u^2C_11|A||x|, and bar_u uC_12|A||A^{-1}||A||x|. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Lemma 4.3]

The conclusion is componentwise; replacing it by a norm inequality is not the same paper claim. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 818, anchor: componentwise convention; PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Lemma 4.3]

The explicit final smallness hypothesis is c_8uκ(A^{-1})≤1/2, with κ(A^{-1})=|| |A||A^{-1}| ||, not a conventional norm condition number. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 820, anchor: κ definition; PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Lemma 4.3]

bar_u must distinguish residual modes exactly: bar_u=u for s.p.r.a. and bar_u=u^2 for d.p.r.a.; d.p.r.a. additionally converts its residual to single precision with relative error bounded by u. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 825, anchor: Lemma 4.1; PDF p. 9, printed p. 824, anchor: residual-precision paragraph]
The algorithm variant is Gaussian elimination with column pivoting, used for both x_1 and every d_m solve. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 824, anchor: Section 4 algorithm]

The result includes m=0 through the artificial initialization x_0=0, r_0=-b, d_0=-x_1; it is not restricted to positive m. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 824, anchor: initialization; PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Lemma 4.3]
No big-O remainder may be added in place of the explicit u^2 and bar_u u terms. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Lemma 4.3]

ambiguities.issue: The anonymous constants are described as bounded by functions of n only, although several displayed definitions contain A and u.
ambiguities.evidence: The convention says c_i and C_i are positive quantities bounded above by functions of n only, while C_2,C_6,C_10,C_11,C_12 visibly contain u, |A|, and |A^{-1}|. [PDF p. 7, printed p. 822, anchor: anonymous-quantity convention; PDF p. 8, printed p. 823, anchor: C_2 definition; PDF p. 11, printed p. 826, anchor: C_6 definition; PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: C_10-C_12 definitions]
ambiguities.impact: The faithful reading is that the displayed quantities are defined using the data and u but are uniformly bounded by n-only functions under the smallness assumptions; they should not silently be replaced by arbitrary constants depending literally only on n.

ambiguities.issue: The scalar rounding model is not fully specified.
ambiguities.evidence: The paper gives relative-error bounds u and u^2 and assumes operations are well defined, but it does not specify radix, rounding direction, tie behavior, underflow, overflow, or an explicit per-operation δ formula. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 818, anchor: Section 2 floating-point model; PDF p. 9, printed p. 824, anchor: residual-precision paragraph]
ambiguities.impact: A formal contract should retain only the stated relative-error bounds and well-definedness assumption rather than choosing an unstated IEEE or round-to-nearest model.

ambiguities.issue: The proof recurrence is displayed without an explicit index range even though it contains q_m and q_0 was never defined.
ambiguities.evidence: The algorithm defines x_0,r_0,d_0 and Lemma 4.1 defines q_{m+1} for m≥0, so q_1 is the first defined q. The proof then displays a recurrence from q_m to q_{m+1}, treats m=0 separately using Lemma 4.1, and proceeds by induction. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 824, anchor: initialization; PDF p. 10, printed p. 825, anchor: Lemma 4.1; PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: proof of Lemma 4.3]
ambiguities.impact: The natural formalization uses the recurrence only for the induction steps with m≥1, while retaining the lemma's conclusion for every m≥0.

ambiguities.issue: The final lemma and its displayed recurrence mention different smallness constants.
ambiguities.evidence: Lemma 4.3 explicitly assumes c_8uκ(A^{-1})≤1/2, whereas the recurrence in its proof is displayed under c_1uκ(A^{-1})≤1/2. The page does not separately state the implication between these conditions. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Lemma 4.3 and proof recurrence]
ambiguities.impact: The source contract must preserve c_8 as the explicit final hypothesis. A formal proof may need to derive the earlier c_1 condition from the constant definitions instead of adding it as a second explicit theorem hypothesis.

ambiguities.issue: The matrix norm extension is described only as being done in the usual way.
ambiguities.evidence: The paper explicitly defines the absolute and normalized vector norm but says only that it is extended to row vectors and matrices in the usual way. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 819, anchor: absolute monotone norm convention]
ambiguities.impact: An implementation should document its induced-matrix-norm interpretation and should not silently substitute a specifically chosen 1-, 2-, or infinity norm.

ambiguities.issue: Column pivoting is identified by its pivot-selection rule, but minor implementation details and pivot ties are not fixed.
ambiguities.evidence: The paper calls column pivoting the variant selecting the largest element of the next column, while the detailed C_1 estimate is said to hold under certain assumptions on minor computational details. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 818, anchor: Section 3 overview; PDF p. 8, printed p. 823, anchor: basic column-pivoted solve result]
ambiguities.impact: The invariant semantic requirement is the stated column-pivoted solve certificate; the passage does not authorize choosing a unique tie-breaking or low-level elimination implementation.

contract_plain_english: For the specified column-pivoted iterative-refinement computation, q_{m+1} is the exact residual obtained after applying the computed correction d_m to x_m but before rounding the new iterate. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 824, anchor: Section 4 algorithm; PDF p. 10, printed p. 825, anchor: Lemma 4.1] Under c_8uκ(A^{-1})≤1/2, every m≥0 satisfies one explicit componentwise four-term bound: a finite iteration term, an n bar_u residual-accumulation term, a u^2 term, and a bar_u u term containing |A||A^{-1}||A||x|. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Lemma 4.3] Here bar_u is u for single-precision residual accumulation and u^2 for double-precision residual accumulation, and no asymptotic remainder is omitted. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 825, anchor: Lemma 4.1; PDF p. 12, printed p. 827, anchor: Lemma 4.3]
